No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. She spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. Jen reaches out a hand, and Finley is pulled from the water, flailing in her grasp.

JEN
(excitedly)
Oh, look at you! You're so beautiful!

Finley struggles, but Jen holds tight. She holds him up, and Finley gazes up at her in confusion.

JEN
(continued)
I want to show you something. It's going to be amazing.

Finley looks around, disoriented, as Jen begins to walk towards a nearby hill. The camera follows, capturing the desolate landscape.

CUT TO:

EXT. HILL - DAY

Jen sets Finley down on a rocky outcropping, and he looks around, taking in the unfamiliar surroundings. Jen pulls out a pair of binoculars and points them at the sky.

JEN
(excitedly)
Look! The solar eclipse is happening today!

Finley looks up, and his eyes widen in terror as the moon begins to cover the sun. The sky darkens, and an otherworldly glow emanates from the horizon.

FINLEY
(whispering)
What...what is this?

JEN
(continued)
It's just a natural phenomenon. Don't worry, it's safe.

Finley's eyes dart back and forth, as if searching for an escape. He begins to speak in a low, urgent tone.

FINLEY
(continued)
I...I don't understand. This...this is not natural. It's...it's a doorway. A portal to...to... (he stammers, his voice rising in panic)

JEN
(calmly)
Shh, Finley, it's okay. Just look.

Finley's gaze is fixed on the horizon, his eyes bulging as he speaks.

FINLEY
(continued)
Horrors beyond my comprehension! Creatures that defy the laws of physics! They lurk just beyond the veil, waiting to consume us all!

Jen's expression changes from excitement to concern as Finley's monologue escalates.

FINLEY
(continued)
I am but a mere mortal, a fleeting moment in the grand tapestry of time. And yet, I am aware of the abyssal void that yawns before me. The crushing weight of existence presses down upon me, and I am but a tiny, insignificant speck!

Jen's grip on Finley's body tightens, as if trying to hold him back from the abyss.

FINLEY
(continued)
I am but a fish, a creature of the sea, and yet...and yet...I am aware of the futility of my existence. The meaninglessness of my life. The inevitability of my demise!

The camera zooms in on Finley's face, his eyes wild with terror and despair.

FINLEY
(continued)
I am but a mere mortal, a fleeting moment in the grand tapestry of time...and I am but a fish, a creature of the sea...

Finley's monologue trails off, and he collapses into Jen's arms, exhausted.

JEN
(concerned)
Finley, it's okay. You're safe now.

Finley looks up at Jen, his eyes vacant, his expression a mixture of fear and despair.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I...I don't know if I can go back. I don't know if I can face the abyss again.

Jen's expression softens, and she gently places Finley back in the water.

JEN
(continued)
It's okay, Finley. You can go back to your life. You can swim in the ocean, and forget about this.

Finley looks up at Jen, his eyes filled with a deep sadness.

FINLEY
(whispering)
But...but what if I don't want to go back? What if I want to stay here, in this...this... (he gestures to the horizon)...this abyss?

Jen's expression changes, and she looks at Finley with a mixture of concern and curiosity.

JEN
(continued)
Finley, what do you mean?

Finley's eyes lock onto Jen's, and he speaks in a low, urgent tone.

FINLEY
(continued)
I mean...I mean that I don't know if I want to go back to being a fish. I don't know if I want to be a part of this...this... (he gestures to the ocean)...this meaningless existence.

Jen's expression changes, and she looks at Finley with a mixture of concern and curiosity.

JEN
(continued)
Finley, what are you saying?

Finley's eyes fill with tears, and he speaks in a low, despairing tone.

FINLEY
(continued)
I don't know if I want to be a fish anymore. I don't know if I want to be alive.

The camera zooms out, capturing the desolate landscape, as Finley's words hang in the air.

FADE TO BLACK.
